name: shushah

fittedAgainst.note: derived from Sentinel-2 and rescaled to measured depths. Not a survey: a derived seabed with a known error rather than an unknown one.

datum: mean sea level; z = 0 is the surface and depth is negative z

heightfield.format: little-endian float32, row major, south to north then west to east

reef.sizesFrom: a draw against the prototype's own size, capped by the depth band; nobody measured any of these

cover.from: Allen Coral Atlas benthic map of this reef, 10 m, CC BY 4.0: over the 0.62 km2 of this 4 km2 site it maps, Rubble 36.5%, Rock 32.3%, Coral/Algae 20.0%, Sand 11.1%; inner reef flat 39.5%, outer reef flat 31.8%, reef slope 13.7%, sheltered slope 12.8%. Coral/Algae is one class and an upper bound on coral cover, not a measurement. No transect has been published for Shushah itself. Held against the northeastern Saudi Red Sea: Lin et al. 2023, Mar. Pollut. Bull. 196:115693 (doi 10.1016/j.marpolbul.2023.115693), visual census and BRUV across the NE Red Sea, mean 36% coral of which 32% stony and 4% soft; and Pisapia, Osman and Johnson 2026, Mar. Pollut. Bull. (doi 10.1016/j.marpolbul.2025.119050), northern Saudi reef sites carrying 42.6% more coral cover than comparable central ones

habitatFrom.why: the place says what it is made of — a survey's habitat polygons, or a composed reef's own parts — rather than this working it out from the shape. 93% of the site is reef habitat and that is a fact about the place, not an inference that failed to discriminate.

coverPaidFor.why: the colony ceiling binds: this reef is built at the density the budget allows and not at the cover its map asks for

beginAt.within: the band a vehicle works a reef in, 8 to 18 m

coverMeasuredBy.over: the reef habitat this place was planted into, which is what a transect figure is cover of
coverMeasuredBy.statistic: all the colony area over all the reef habitat, saturated as 1 - exp(-A/G) because colonies are scattered rather than tiled

assemblage.name: red-sea
assemblage.from: The platform's Red Sea mix, derived from Khalil, Bouwmeester and Berumen 2017 (PeerJ 5:e3410) line-intercept transects off Thuwal, 600 km south: Porites massive, Pocillopora branching, Acropora table on the slope. Pisapia, Osman and Johnson 2026 (Mar. Pollut. Bull., doi 10.1016/j.marpolbul.2025.119050) surveyed the same three genera on northern (NEOM-region) reef crests and slopes and found them present with larger massive Porites on the crest and more Pocillopora than the central reefs, so the mix stands for the north with those two shifts unmodelled; a NEOM transect with genus shares should replace it

beginBecause: the best reef within the band a vehicle works a reef in, 8 to 18 m, three metres off the bottom (87% cover at 14 m)

ground.hardnessFrom: habitat polygons from a survey of this place, and the slope and relief of the seabed where the survey did not reach
ground.colourFrom: orthomosaic and habitat classes from a survey

waterBakedFrom.why: no per-pixel value reaches an expression in this renderer, so how much of each colour survives the swim to the camera is worked out here and written into a map. A texture lookup is the thing that does work. It is measured from where dives begin: a vehicle that swims far from this point carries water measured from this point, and a different water type needs this run again.

water.from: Kd(PAR) 0.049-0.119 per metre at the pelagic station offshore of KAUST: Overmans & Agusti 2020, Front. Mar. Sci. 7:111. The water off Duba, 70 km south of Shushah, is clearer still (Kd(PAR) 0.039 per metre, Overmans & Agusti 2019, Photochem. Photobiol. 95:1267, which is Jerlov IA), but the renderer has only been held against IB and 1C and rendered IA as a white-out; IB is the nearest calibrated type and errs towards more attenuation than the measurement

life.perSquareMetreFrom: visual census of reef fish over ~8 cm, order 0.05-0.2 per m2; not measured at this site
